To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the RSV‐mediated expression of ICAM-1 on lung epithelial cells is inhibited by PPARγ agonist treatment.

PPAR‐γ ligands reduce RSV‐inducible ICAM‐1‐expression and adhesion of monocytoid cells to RSV‐exposed lung epithelial cells, and that the anti‐inflammatory effect of PPAR‐γ activation is due to a reduced NF‐κB activation.
PPAR‐γ‐agonists inhibit RSV‐inducible expression of ICAM-1 in lung epithelial cells by interfering with the NF-κB pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the anti‐inflammatory potential of PPAR‐γ ligands in RSV infection.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms involved in the regulation of RSV‐induction of ICAM‐ 1 in human lung cells and the potential therapeutic implications of these mechanisms.
the identification of a novel class of anti‐inflammatory compounds that may be of therapeutic value in the course of RSV infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PPAR‐γ is an anti‐inflammatory transcriptional factor that may be a new therapeutic target for the treatment of severe RSV infection.
PPAR‐γ ligands might be useful for the treatment of RSV infection in humans.
PPAR‐γ ligands might be useful in the treatment of RSV‐induction of ICAM‐mediated inflammation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RSV‐infuced ICAM‐l expression on human airway epithelial cells is inhibited by PPAR‐γ ligands and that PPAR‐γ might therefore be a potential target for the development of new anti‐RSV‐therapies.
PPARγ ligands are able to modulate the inflammatory response during respiratory syncytial viral infection.

RSV‐induction of ICAM‐ 1 expression in lung epithelial cells can be modulated by PPAR‐γ ligands, resulting in a reduced binding activity of NF‐κB and a reduced ICAM‐ 2 mRNA level and ICAM‐1 protein expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PPAR‐γ ligands may be used to reduce inflammation during RSV infection.
PPAR‐γ ligands are potent inhibitors of RSV‐inducible ICAM‐1 and that this may be an effective approach to the development of novel antiviral and antiphlogistic therapy.
PPAR‐γ ligands may be useful in the treatment of severe RSV infection.
